memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When Peleg had lived 30 years, he became the father of Reu... When Reu had lived 32 years, he became the father of Serug... When Serug had lived 30 years, he became the father of Nahor... - Gen 11:18-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The generations roll on - Reu, Serug, Nahor. With each name, we draw a step closer to Abraham, the man through whom God would bless all nations. These people had no idea what was coming. They lived their lives never knowing that their family line was carrying the hope of the world toward a promise none of them would see.

That is a striking thought. God's promises often span far beyond a single lifetime. These men were part of something magnificent, yet they saw only their small portion of it. They were faithful links in a chain whose end they could not glimpse.

We are often the same. We long to see the fruit of our prayers, our labour, our faithfulness. But some of what God is doing through us will only be seen by those who come long after us. The seeds we plant may be harvested by our grandchildren, or by people we never meet.

Scripture honours those who died "living by faith... They did not receive the things promised; they only saw them and welcomed them from a distance" (Heb 11:13). That is no small thing - it is faith at its purest. Be faithful in your generation, even if you never see where it leads. God's promises are worth serving, even from a distance. The line that ran through Serug and Nahor ran on to Christ, and God's purposes for your faithfulness may reach further than you know.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Can you be faithful even without seeing the fruit in your lifetime?
- What are you doing now whose fruit may only be seen by later generations?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me be faithful in my generation, even when I cannot see where it leads. Give me faith to serve promises whose fruit may come long after me, trusting Your purposes reach further than my sight.
Amen.
